slides.title: Short track boots that actually fit
slides.sub: Sizing, moulding and the first three sessions

slides.title: Measure at the end of the day
slides.body: Stand with your heel against a wall and mark your longest toe. Measure both feet, work from the larger one, and note the width across the ball.

slides.title: Snug is the right feeling
slides.body: Toes brush the front when standing and pull back in a skating position. A heel that lifts more than a couple of millimetres means the boot is too big.

slides.title: Between sizes? Take the smaller one
slides.body: A slightly snug boot settles after moulding. One that is slightly large will never get smaller. The same goes for growing juniors.

slides.title: Moulding fixes shape, not size
slides.caption: What a heat mould can change, and what only the right size fixes.

slides.title: Mould in a skating posture
slides.body: Wear your race socks, do not over tighten the laces, drive the knee forward and let the boot cool completely before it comes off.

slides.title: Read your first three sessions
slides.body: One sharp spot is a missed bony area. Heel lift on a hard push is a volume problem. Numbness means loosen the laces before you skate on.
